name: Scroll area
summary: A box with thin themed scrollbars whose edges fade where more content waits, vertically or sideways.
description: Use it for a long list inside a card or a row of chips that would not fit. Do not wrap whole pages in it; let the page scroll normally.

classes.name: v-scroll
classes.description: Scrolls vertically up to --v-scroll-max (default 20rem), with fading top and bottom edges.

classes.name: v-scroll-x
classes.description: Scrolls sideways instead, fading the start and end edges (mirrored in right-to-left).

states.description: Lets keyboard users focus the area and scroll it with the arrow keys. The fade drops while focused so the ring is never masked.
With aria-label or aria-labelledby, names the area for screen readers.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the area when it has tabindex="0".

a11y: An area that overflows needs tabindex="0", role="region" and a label, or keyboard users cannot reach the hidden part.
The fade is a scroll-driven enhancement; without support the area simply scrolls.
overscroll-behavior: contain stops the page from scrolling when the area reaches its end.

Release notes

  • Tables gain a sticky header and a dense variant.
  • Timeline markers take an icon, an avatar or a dot.
  • Prose styles CMS output with no classes at all.
  • Code blocks number their lines with CSS counters.
  • Testimonials show a rating that screen readers announce.
  • Pricing cards line their buttons up across a row.
  • Logo clouds stay monochrome until you hover them.
  • Scroll areas fade their edges where more content waits.
  • Every component reads its colours from tokens.
  • Right-to-left layouts work through logical properties.
